Proposed supply agreement represents a significant step in Burcon's commercial expansion and provides greater visibility into 2027 revenue growth

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Burcon NutraScience Corporation (TSX: BU) (OTCQB: BRCNF) ("Burcon" or the "Company"), a global technology leader in plant-based protein innovation, today announced that it has signed a non-binding letter of intent ("LOI") with an established consumer packaged goods ("CPG") company and existing customer for the supply of up to US$6 million of Burcon's protein ingredients in calendar 2027. The parties are negotiating the final terms a definitive supply agreement.

The proposed agreement represents a significant expansion of an existing customer relationship and reflects growing commercial adoption of Burcon's protein ingredients. If realized, the anticipated purchase volumes will represent a meaningful increase in Burcon's commercial revenue and support its plans to scale production in 2027.

"We are seeing commercial adoption accelerate as customers move from initial product validation to increasingly significant commercial opportunities," said Kip Underwood, Chief Executive Officer. "This LOI reflects the growing value our differentiated protein technology delivers to mainstream food and beverage companies. The potential scale of this expanded customer relationship reinforces our confidence in our 2027 growth objectives and the opportunity beyond."

The potential US$6 million sales in calendar 2027 is based on anticipated customer requirements and remains subject to execution of a definitive supply agreement, production schedules, and other commercial conditions. The LOI is non-binding, and the anticipated sales do not represent a guaranteed minimum purchase commitment.

Burcon continues to advance its manufacturing capabilities and operational reliability to support anticipated customer demand. The Company remains focused on commercial execution, expanding customer adoption, and scaling production to capture the growing opportunity for specialty plant-based protein ingredients.

About Burcon NutraScience Corporation

Burcon is a global technology leader in plant-based proteins for food and beverage applications. The Company has developed a portfolio of high-performance protein ingredients, including Peazzaz® pea proteins, FavaPro® fava proteins and Puratein® canola proteins, and is focused on commercializing its technologies through manufacturing partnerships and growing customer adoption worldwide. http://www.burcon.ca/

Aether Compute will utilize Cho Thavee Public Company Limited's existing approximately 14-acre factory site in Khon Kaen, with a reported 0.85 MW of existing power capacity, as the proposed foundation for an AI data center joint venture

  • The partnership is intended to combine CHO's industrial real estate, reported existing power and local operating experience with Aether Compute's technical and delivery capabilities.

  • Aether to hold a 47.5% interest in the proposed joint venture, alongside opportunities to support the project by providing infrastructure development, deployment and managed services.

  • CHO to contribute the site access through below-market long-term leases and purchase options.

  • Advance Capital Partners to support initial project setup, regulatory coordination and capital-raising activities.

New York, New York--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Aether Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: ATHR) ("Aether" or the "Company"), a technology holding company focused on expanding its AI infrastructure and enterprise technology services business through its Aether Compute subsidiary, today announced that it has entered into a binding tripartite framework agreement with Cho Thavee Public Company Limited (SET: CHO) ("CHO") and Advance Capital Partners Limited ("ACP"), a Singapore-based capital partner, establishing the principal terms for a proposed joint venture to develop and operate an AI data center project in Khon Kaen, Thailand.

Founded in 1994 and headquartered in Khon Kaen, CHO is a Thai manufacturer of trailers, specialty vehicles and transit buses. Aether Compute identified CHO's existing factory as a strong starting point for AI infrastructure development in Thailand and proposed the joint venture to CHO. The partnership combines CHO's industrial real estate, existing power and local operating experience with Aether Compute's technical and delivery capabilities, with potential room for expansion within the site.

The proposed initial phase would target the approximately 14-acre factory site, which has reported existing power capacity of 0.85 MW, subject to site assessment and required approvals. This phased approach could allow initial development to proceed around available resources, with any additional capacity pursued only as customer demand, power availability, financing and project economics support.

Under the framework agreement, CHO would contribute the proposed site to the joint venture through below-market long-term site leases and purchase options, along with its existing power and local operating experience, with site selection and development phasing subject to assessment and required project approvals.

Aether Compute would contribute enterprise technology expertise and support the project through AetherMDC infrastructure planning and deployment services and its AetherPod modular data center offering. Its anticipated role would extend from configuring and integrating systems to providing platform licensing and ongoing managed services.

Upon formation of the joint venture, Aether and CHO would each hold 47.5% of the joint venture and ACP would hold the remaining 5% in connection with its role in facilitating initial setup, regulatory coordination and capital-raising activities during the implementation phase. The joint venture is expected to seek third-party financing for project expenditures, and Aether would have no obligation to fund or guarantee those expenditures absent a separate written commitment. There can be no assurance that such financing will be available on acceptable terms or at all.

"This project represents an opportunity for Aether Compute to extend its enterprise technology services into a broader infrastructure development role, along with a potential path to recurring platform and service revenue," said Nicolas Lin, Chief Executive Officer of Aether Holdings. "The proposed structure lets us take part in AI infrastructure development with limited use of our balance sheet. We see an opportunity to pair our technical and delivery capabilities with local industrial assets to address enterprise and AI computing requirements, and we believe CHO can provide a practical starting point in Thailand."

"The factory in Khon Kaen offers an opportunity to put our existing industrial space and available power to work as a foundation for AI computing infrastructure," said Suradech Taweesaengsakulthai, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of CHO Thavee. "Working with Aether Compute, we aim to begin with an initial deployment and make greater use of the site's available space as demand grows. This partnership is intended to combine our facilities and local experience with Aether's technical capabilities to develop and manage that infrastructure."

About Aether Compute

Aether Compute is the AI infrastructure business of Aether Holdings, focused on modular data center solutions, infrastructure design and deployment, managed IT services and strategic technology partnerships supporting AI, enterprise and other compute-intensive workloads.

About Aether Holdings, Inc.

Aether Holdings, Inc. is a vertically integrated technology holding company operating across AI-powered investor intelligence, digital media and emerging infrastructure technologies. Through its proprietary portfolio optimization and market intelligence platforms, together with its curated financial publications, Aether applies advanced analytics and data science to deliver timely market analysis and actionable insights to retail and institutional investors.

Across its portfolio, the Company develops technology and infrastructure solutions designed to support data-intensive applications and broaden access to advanced digital tools.

Actively managed IncomeQ Nasdaq-100® Premium Income ETF seeks to generate income by selling put options on individual stocks and index-related instruments while pursuing outperformance over a full market cycle.

NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Quantify Funds today announced the launch of the IncomeQ Nasdaq-100® Premium Income ETF (IQQI), an actively managed exchange-traded fund designed to pursue capital appreciation and current income through a differentiated approach to options investing.

The fund seeks exposure to the growth potential of the Nasdaq-100® while pursuing weekly cash distributions without relying on covered calls that limit gains above a predetermined strike price. It seeks to outperform the Nasdaq-100® over a full market cycle, although neither outperformance nor distributions are guaranteed.

IQQI takes a different approach to generating options income. Rather than primarily selling call options against its market exposure, the fund sells put options and put spreads on selected individual stocks and Nasdaq-100® -related instruments. Its investment managers actively evaluate where options premiums appear attractive relative to the risks assumed.

“Investors shouldn't have to look at income and growth as completely separate objectives,” said David Dziekanski, Co-Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chief Investment Officer of Quantify Funds. “The question we asked was whether there is another way to pursue both without automatically giving up upside in strong markets. IQQI reflects our belief that investment innovation starts by challenging familiar trade-offs and understanding the risks behind a different approach.”

Finding Opportunity in the Demand for Protection

A central element of IQQI's investment thesis is that investors do not always purchase options for the same reasons.

Company founders, executives and other concentrated shareholders may seek protection against declines in individual stocks because of the potential financial consequences of a large loss. That demand can influence options pricing, potentially creating opportunities for investors willing to assume the corresponding downside risk.

IQQI seeks to evaluate these opportunities through active options management, selling puts or put spreads on individual stocks where the investment team believes the premiums provide attractive compensation for the risk. The fund can also use options on the Nasdaq-100® or related ETFs when those opportunities appear more attractive.

“Options pricing reflects more than a forecast of where a stock is headed. It also reflects why investors want protection,” said Zed Francis, Co-Founder and Chief Investment Officer of Convexitas. “Concentrated shareholders and institutions may have reasons to hedge that go beyond short-term market expectations. Our focus is on evaluating what investors are willing to pay for that protection and whether the compensation justifies the risk of providing it.”

An Alternative Balance of Growth, Income and Risk

IQQI seeks to maintain uncapped upside exposure to the Nasdaq-100® while generating options premiums that may support weekly distributions. Its actively managed approach allows the investment team to adjust positions based on changing market conditions, volatility and options pricing.

That strategy involves meaningful trade-offs. Selling put options creates additional downside exposure, and the fund can experience losses greater than those of the Nasdaq-100 during sharp market declines. The fund's performance can also differ from the index because of its holdings, derivatives, fees and trading costs.

Weekly distributions are not guaranteed, may fluctuate and may include return of capital rather than investment profits.

IQQI is part of Quantify Funds' broader commitment to developing investment strategies through disciplined research, innovation and transparency about investment risk.

November 19, 2026 – TheNewswire - Timmins, Ontario – Melkior Resources Inc. ("Melkior" or the "Company") (TSXV: MKR) (OTCQB: MKRIF) is pleased to announce that drilling has commenced on its 12-hole, approximately 4,400-metre diamond drill program at the Beschefer East Project (the "Project") in the Northern Abitibi Greenstone Belt, located approximately 90 km west of Matagami and 100 km north of La Sarre, Québec.

Highlights

  • The program will be completed in two phases and is designed to test four target areas characterized by historical gold and polymetallic mineralization associated with coincident induced polarization ("IP") chargeability anomalies, electromagnetic ("EM") conductors and magnetic features. Planned hole lengths range from approximately 250 to 700 metres. 

  • Phase 1 (fall 2026): four holes totalling approximately 1,400 metres testing the interpreted northern extension of the B14 gold trend along a north-south magnetic and IP chargeability corridor. 

  • Historical intercepts in the Phase 1 target area include 2.1 g/t Au over 5.4 metres, including 7.9 g/t Au over 0.9 metres, in hole 1172-13-40 and 2.03 g/t Au over 6.1 metres in hole 1172-99-30. 

  • Phase 2 (winter 2027): eight holes totalling approximately 3,065 metres testing the eastern extensions of the B14 gold trend and the B26 gold-base metal volcanogenic massive sulphide ("VMS") trend, as well as structurally controlled gold targets along the Enjalran-Brouillan Group contact. 

  • Forage DCB Inc., a Québec-based drilling contractor, has mobilized to the property and Phase 1 drilling is now underway. Phase 1 is expected to take approximately three to four weeks, with assay results anticipated in the first quarter of 2027. 

Management Commentary

Bernard Deluce, CEO and Director, commented:

"The Beschefer East Project hosts several underexplored geophysical and geological targets supported by historical drilling and extensive geophysical coverage. This program has been designed to test priority gold and polymetallic targets identified by previous operators. We expect it to provide important information on the continuity and extent of the mineralized systems across the property and to help advance several prospective target areas."

Phase 1 comprises four drill holes, BEE-20, BEE-39, BEE-40 and BEE-41, located south of the main access road. The holes are designed to evaluate the interpreted northern extension of the B14 gold mineralized trend along a north-south magnetic and IP chargeability corridor.

2027 Winter Drill Program (Phase 2)

Phase 2 is expected to comprise eight drill holes totalling approximately 3,065 metres and will target multiple mineralized trends identified through historical drilling and geophysical surveys.

Holes BEE-18, BEE-19, BEE-26 and BEE-27 are designed to test the interpreted eastern extension of the B14 gold trend, while hole BEE-42 will evaluate the extension of the B26 gold-base metal VMS trend. These targets are supported by historical drill results and coincident IP and magnetic anomalies.

Hole BEE-35 is planned to verify and follow up on historical Cu-Zn-Ag mineralization intersected by Noramco in hole H-1432-091, which returned 0.11% Cu, 0.24% Zn and 0.90 g/t Ag over 24.4 metres, including 0.61% Cu, 0.30% Zn and 6.6 g/t Ag over 6.0 metres.

Holes BEE-13 and BEE-14 will test gold targets associated with graphitic argillites along the Enjalran-Brouillan Group contact zone. These targets coincide with elevated IP chargeability responses and historical drilling that returned 3.45 g/t Au over 1.5 metres in hole 1172-95-02, and 3.37 g/t Au over 1.3 metres and 2.06 g/t Au over 2.5 metres in hole 1172-98-24.

About the Beschefer East Project

On June 14, 2023, the Company entered into an option agreement on the Project to earn a 100% interest over three years from SOQUEM Inc. ("SOQUEM") (see news release dated June 14, 2023). In March 2026, the option agreement was amended to extend the deadline for completing the cumulative exploration expenditure requirement of $1,500,000 by one year, from July 3, 2026, to July 3, 2027. All other terms of the option agreement remain unchanged.

The Project is located within the prospective yet underexplored Selbaie mining camp and comprises 55 mining claims covering 2,906 hectares.

Between 1992 and 2012, SOQUEM completed systematic exploration on the property, including more than 300 line-kilometres of geophysical surveys and 11,200 metres of diamond drilling in 42 holes.

In early 2025, Melkior completed a six-hole, 1,050-metre drill program testing a previously undrilled area in the east-central part of the property, where a 1,780-sample bio-geochemical (spruce bark MMI) survey had outlined five gold-polymetallic anomalies coincident with IP-EM conductors. Hole MKR-BE-2024-001 intersected 5.1 g/t Au, 0.95% Cu and 0.67% Zn over 0.9 metres and 7.5 g/t Au over 1.3 metres, confirming an 800-metre copper-gold mineralized horizon (see news release dated July 17, 2025).

Notable historical gold intersections from the northern powerline area include hole 1172-99-30, which intersected multiple mineralized zones grading between 2 and 5 g/t Au over intervals of 0.5 to 6.0 metres within a broader 70-metre mineralized corridor. Hole 1172-13-40 returned 2.1 g/t Au over 5.4 metres, including 7.9 g/t Au over 0.9 metres.

Gold mineralization is associated with networks of centimetre-scale quartz-carbonate veins hosted in felsic to intermediate volcanic rocks affected by varying degrees of pervasive alteration and minor pyrite. In the southern portion of the property, gold and base metal mineralization occurs within deformed, carbonate-altered andesites. Historical drilling also identified anomalous copper mineralization, including 0.26% Cu over 4.8 metres in hole 1172-98-24 and 0.24% Cu over 4.0 metres in hole 1172-99-30.

Sampling and Analytical Procedures

Drill core will be NQ in size. Core will be logged and sampled by Company geologists, with sampled intervals sawn in half; one half will be sent for analysis and the other retained for future reference. Samples will be delivered under chain-of-custody protocols to an independent, accredited commercial laboratory and analyzed for gold by fire assay with atomic absorption finish. Samples returning greater than 10 g/t Au will be re-analyzed by fire assay with gravimetric finish, and intervals containing visible gold will be analyzed by metallic screen fire assay.

Quality Assurance and Quality Control

The Company will implement a quality assurance and quality control ("QA/QC") program that includes the systematic insertion of certified reference materials, blank samples and duplicate samples into the sample stream. QA/QC results will be monitored by the Company's technical staff to evaluate analytical accuracy, contamination and precision.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Martin Ethier, P.Geo., a consultant to Melkior Resources Inc. and a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.

Board Update

Melkior also announces that Jonathon Deluce has resigned as a director of the Company, effective November 17, 2026. The Board thanks Mr. Deluce for his contributions to the Company and wishes him continued success.

About Melkior Resources

Melkior Resources Inc. is a Canadian mineral exploration company focused on the discovery and advancement of gold projects in the prolific mining jurisdictions of Ontario and Québec. The Company is committed to creating shareholder value through disciplined, technically driven exploration and the systematic evaluation of high-potential mineral assets.

Melkior's core portfolio is anchored by the Carscallen Gold Project, located in the heart of the Timmins Gold Camp, one of Canada's most productive gold districts. The Company also holds the Val-d'Or Project, an option on the Genex Project, and an option to earn a 100% interest in the Beschefer East Project, all strategically positioned within the highly prospective Abitibi Greenstone Belt, a world-renowned mining region that hosts numerous significant gold and base metal deposits.

SOQUEM is a mineral exploration company and a subsidiary of Investissement Québec. Its mission is to explore, discover, and develop Quebec’s mineral resources.   • Two positive Phase 3 studies showed CAPLYTA significantly reduced manic symptoms versus placebo as early as Day 3, with improvement sustained through Week 3
  • As the first and only FDA-approved treatment for both bipolar I and II depression in adults as a monotherapy and adjunctive therapy, filing seeks to expand CAPLYTA for the treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder
  • Approval would mark the fifth approved use of CAPLYTA in adults, building on its robust efficacy and established safety and tolerability profile across major depressive disorder, bipolar depression and schizophrenia

NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced the submission of a supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seeking the approval of CAPLYTA (lumateperone) for the treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults. The submission is supported by two pivotal Phase 3 studies in which CAPLYTA significantly reduced manic symptoms versus placebo as early as Day 3, with improvement sustained through Week 3. If approved, bipolar mania would become the fifth approved use for CAPLYTA in adults.

An estimated 11 million U.S. adults experience bipolar disorder at some point in their lives.1 For people living with bipolar I disorder, manic episodes can escalate rapidly, disrupting daily life and putting their safety, relationships, career, and financial wellbeing at risk—and often are severe enough to require hospitalization.2,3

"For people experiencing acute mania, rapid symptom improvement and tolerability are both critical treatment considerations," said John C. Reed, M.D., Ph.D., Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine, R&D, Johnson & Johnson. "Our Phase 3 results demonstrate the potential for CAPLYTA to address these needs, and this submission advances our ambition to provide a foundational treatment that can support patients across the evolving course of serious psychiatric disorders."

Pivotal Phase 3 Study Results 
The sNDA submission is based on positive results from Study 451 and Study 452, two pivotal Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies of once-daily CAPLYTA 42 mg versus placebo in adults with manic episodes, with or without mixed features, associated with bipolar I disorder. In both studies, CAPLYTA met the primary and key secondary endpoints, demonstrating significant and rapid improvement in bipolar mania symptoms and overall illness severity versus placebo. Improvement in manic symptoms was observed as early as Day 3, following two days of treatment. CAPLYTA was well tolerated, with low rates of discontinuation and a safety profile consistent with prior studies.4,5 

CAPLYTA is approved in adults living with depressive episodes associated with bipolar I or II disorder as monotherapy or adjunctive therapy, major depressive disorder as adjunctive therapy with antidepressants and schizophrenia. It is not approved for the treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder.

ABOUT BIPOLAR MANIA
An estimated 11 million U.S. adults experience bipolar disorder at some point in their lives.1 Mania is a defining feature of bipolar I disorder—a period of abnormally elevated or irritable mood and/or increased energy or activity that most people experience alongside depressive episodes over the course of the illness.6 Symptoms of mania can include grandiosity, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, distractibility, and risk-taking behavior.6 Manic episodes can escalate quickly, often requiring hospitalization for safety and treatment.7 These noticeable behavioral changes often differ markedly from an individual's baseline and can have serious consequences for a person's safety, relationships, career, and finances, contributing to its standing as one of the leading causes of disability worldwide.2 Rapid and sustained control of manic symptoms remains an important treatment goal in the management of bipolar I disorder.

ABOUT STUDY 451 and STUDY 452
Studies 451 and 452 are two positive randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 studies of lumateperone versus placebo in adults with manic episodes, with or without mixed features, associated with bipolar I disorder. In each study, patients were randomized to receive once-daily lumateperone 42 mg or placebo for three weeks. The primary endpoint of each study was change from baseline in Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) total score at Week 3, and the key secondary endpoint was change from baseline in Clinical Global Impression–Severity (CGI-S) score at Week 3.

ABOUT CAPLYTA (lumateperone)
CAPLYTA is an oral, once daily atypical antipsychotic approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in adults for the treatment of depressive episodes associated with bipolar I or II disorder (bipolar depression), as monotherapy or as adjunctive therapy with lithium or valproate; for the treatment of schizophrenia; and as adjunctive therapy with antidepressants for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD).

CAPLYTA is not approved for the treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder.

While the mechanism of action of CAPLYTA is unknown, the efficacy of CAPLYTA could be mediated through a combination of antagonist activity at central serotonin 5-HT2A receptors and partial agonist activity at central dopamine D2 receptors.

CAPLYTA IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is CAPLYTA (lumateperone)?

CAPLYTA (lumateperone) is a prescription medicine used in adults along with an antidepressant to treat major depressive disorder (MDD); to treat depressive episodes associated with bipolar I or bipolar II disorder (bipolar depression) alone or with lithium or valproate; or to treat schizophrenia. It is not known if CAPLYTA is safe and effective in children.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about CAPLYTA?

  • Medicines like CAPLYTA can raise the risk of death in elderly people who have lost touch with reality (psychosis) due to confusion and memory loss (dementia). CAPLYTA is not approved for treating people with dementia-related psychosis.
  • CAPLYTA and antidepressant medicines increase the risk of suicidal thoughts and actions in people 24 years of age and younger, especially within the first few months of treatment or when the dose is changed. Depression and other serious mental illnesses are the most important causes of suicidal thoughts and actions.
    • Patients and their families or caregivers should watch for new or worsening depression symptoms, especially sudden changes in mood, behaviors, thoughts, or feelings. This is very important when CAPLYTA or an antidepressant medicine is started or when the dose is changed.
    • Report any changes in these symptoms to your healthcare provider immediately.

      • thoughts about suicide or dying
      • acting aggressive, being angry or violent
      • new or worse anxiety
      • suicide attempts

  • new or worse depression
  • an extreme increase in activity and talking (mania)
  • panic attacks
  • new or worse irritability

  • feeling very agitated or restless 
  • trouble sleeping
  • acting on dangerous impulses
  • other unusual changes in behavior or mood

Do not take CAPLYTA if you are allergic to any of its ingredients. Get emergency medical help if you are having an allergic reaction (e.g., rash, itching, hives, swelling of the tongue, lip, face, or throat).

What are the possible side effects of CAPLYTA?

CAPLYTA may cause serious side effects, including:

  • Stroke (cerebrovascular problems) in elderly people with dementia-related psychosis that can lead to death.
  • Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS): high fever, confusion, changes in your breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure, stiff muscles, and increased sweating; these may be symptoms of a rare but potentially fatal condition. Contact your healthcare provider or go to the emergency room if you experience signs and symptoms of NMS.
  • Uncontrolled body movements (tardive dyskinesia, TD) in your face, tongue, or other body parts. TD may not go away, even if you stop taking CAPLYTA. It may also occur after you stop taking CAPLYTA.
  • Problems with your metabolism including high blood sugar, diabetes, increased fat (cholesterol and triglyceride) levels in your blood and weight gain. Your healthcare provider should check your blood sugar, fat levels, and weight before you start and during your treatment with CAPLYTA.
    • Extremely high blood sugar levels can lead to coma or death. Call your healthcare provider if you have any of the following symptoms of high blood sugar: feeling very thirsty, hungry, sick to your stomach, needing to urinate more than usual, weak/tired, or confused, or your breath smells fruity.
  • Low white blood cell count. Your healthcare provider may do blood tests during the first few months of treatment with CAPLYTA.
  • Decreased blood pressure (orthostatic hypotension). You may feel lightheaded, dizzy, or faint when you rise too quickly from a sitting or lying position.
  • Falls. CAPLYTA may make you sleepy or dizzy, may cause a decrease in your blood pressure when changing position (orthostatic hypotension), and can slow your thinking and motor skills which may lead to falls that can cause broken bones or other injuries.
  • Seizures (convulsions).
  • Sleepiness, drowsiness, feeling tired, difficulty thinking and doing normal activities. Until you know how CAPLYTA affects you, do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do other dangerous activities.
  • Problems controlling your body temperature so that you feel too warm. Avoid getting overheated or dehydrated while taking CAPLYTA.
  • Difficulty swallowing that can cause food or liquid to get into the lungs.

The most common side effects of CAPLYTA include sleepiness, dizziness, nausea, dry mouth, feeling tired, and diarrhea.

These are not all the possible side effects of CAPLYTA.

Before taking CAPLYTA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you: have or have had heart problems or a stroke, high or low blood pressure, diabetes, or high blood sugar, problems with cholesterol, have or have had a low white blood cell count, seizures (convulsions), or kidney or liver problems.

CAPLYTA may cause fertility problems in females and males. You should notify your healthcare provider if you become pregnant or intend to become pregnant while taking CAPLYTA. There is a pregnancy registry for females who are exposed to CAPLYTA during pregnancy. CAPLYTA may cause abnormal involuntary movements and/or withdrawal symptoms in newborn babies exposed to CAPLYTA during the third trimester. Talk to your healthcare provider if you breastfeed or are planning to breastfeed as CAPLYTA passes into breast milk.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you're taking. CAPLYTA may affect the way other medicines work, and other medicines may affect how CAPLYTA works, causing possible serious side effects. Do not start or stop any medicines while taking CAPLYTA without talking to your healthcare provider. You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs. Contact Intra-Cellular Therapies, Inc. at 1-800-526-7736 or FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088 or www.fda.gov/medwatch.

CAPLYTA is available in 42 mg, 21 mg, and 10.5 mg capsules.

DALLAS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- enCore Energy Corp. (NASDAQ: EU; TSXV: EU) (the "Company" or "enCore") is pleased to announce that the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality ("TCEQ") has issued the Production Area Authorization ("PAA") for the first wellfield ("PAA-1") at the Company's 100% owned Upper Spring Creek In-Situ Recovery ("ISR") Uranium Project ("USC") in South Texas.

Highlights

  • Final authorization received: TCEQ issued PAA-1 for USC within the Company's previously disclosed timeline.
  • Plans to begin extraction:  The Company is making final inspections and expect oxygenated water injection and uranium extraction to begin the first week of December.
  • One remaining step to full-scale operations: The Company is working on getting final approval to operate the Waste Disposal Well (WDW-467) at USC, which will handle the saline water stream generated by wellfield operations. The WDW is fully constructed with approval expected in December.

"Receiving the final authorization for Upper Spring Creek is an important milestone for enCore," said Rich Little, Chief Executive Officer. "The plant and wellfield are built and ready, and our team is focused on completing the last regulatory step. Once the Waste Disposal Well is approved, we expect to bring the wellfield up to full-scale operations and begin delivering the growth in extraction that our South Texas investments were designed to provide."

Upper Spring Creek Permitting Update

PAA-1 authorizes uranium extraction within the first defined wellfield area at USC and is the final wellfield permit required for injection and recovery. The Satellite Ion Exchange ("IX") Plant and first wellfield were constructed ahead of the authorization.

ISR operations recover slightly more solution from a wellfield than is injected in order to keep wellfield solutions contained. This excess saline water, known as the bleed stream, is disposed of through a permitted deep disposal well. The WDW at USC has been constructed for this purpose, and TCEQ approval to operate it is the remaining step before the wellfield can be brought up to its designed operating rates. The Company expects to receive this approval in December and will update the market when the wellfield moves to full-scale operations.

USC is the largest satellite facility the Company has built to date. Uranium-loaded resin from the Satellite IX Plant will be trucked to the Rosita CPP, where it will be processed into yellowcake.

About the Upper Spring Creek ISR Project

The 100% Company-owned Project consists of a Satellite IX Plant and wellfield and is a key component of enCore's larger South Texas Uranium Project. This satellite facility will operate in conjunction with multiple future potential production units within the historic Clay West uranium district. The Project was previously held by Signal Equities LLC, which previously had licensed and permitted the property including the aquifer exemption as an ISR uranium project prior to 2020. The Company acquired the Project in December 2020. The uranium-mineralized sands at the Project lie within the Oakville Formation at depths typically between 300 and 450 feet below surface, allowing for efficient and economical uranium recovery with ISR methods.

LITTLE ROCK, Ark., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Inuvo, Inc. (NYSE American: INUV), a provider of artificial intelligence-driven advertising technology, today announced the appointment of Retired Rear Admiral Tim Flynn and Larissa Smith as strategic advisors to accelerate the expansion of the company’s government and defense verticals.

In their new roles, Flynn and Smith will focus on deploying Inuvo’s proprietary IntentKey® AI signal intelligence to solve one of the nation's most pressing national security challenges: the urgent recruitment of skilled labor across U.S. shipbuilders, shipyards, the broader Defense Industrial Base, and government adjacent opportunities.

Operating in a hyper-competitive talent landscape, shipbuilders, defense contractors and government agencies face historic workforce shortfalls in specialized trades and technical roles. Each is competing directly against massive commercial infrastructure demands, including rapid data center buildouts, for the exact same pool of skilled workers. By utilizing IntentKey’s privacy-compliant, contextual intent modeling—which identifies and reaches high-propensity audiences without relying on personal data or cookies—Inuvo aims to dramatically accelerate hiring pipelines for shipbuilders, prime contractors, sub-tier suppliers, and government recruitment initiatives.

"The Defense Industrial Base and our armed forces are facing an unprecedented demand for skilled talent, and they are fighting for the exact same technicians, engineers, and tradespeople being recruited for large-scale data center buildouts," said Rob Buchner, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Inuvo. "Traditional recruitment methods simply aren't moving fast enough to close the gap. Rear Admiral Flynn and Larissa Smith bring unmatched operational insight and deep relationships across the defense ecosystem, and their guidance will be instrumental as we position IntentKey as the premier intelligence engine for high-stakes workforce acquisition."

Retired Rear Admiral Tim Flynn brings decades of distinguished naval leadership, operational command, and strategic acquisition experience to Inuvo. Having navigated complex maritime readiness and force-generation challenges throughout his career, Rear Admiral Flynn possesses an intimate understanding of the staffing bottlenecks facing naval shipyards and defense infrastructure. He will advise Inuvo on aligning its AI capabilities with the immediate mission-critical needs of military commands and public-sector agencies.

"Maintaining maritime and defense readiness depends directly on our ability to attract and retain a world-class skilled workforce," said Retired Rear Admiral Tim Flynn. "Inuvo’s IntentKey technology offers a fundamentally smarter way to identify and engage individuals with the exact aptitudes and motivations required to serve in our shipbuilding, ship maintenance and uniform ranks. I look forward to helping bring this capability to the forefront of defense talent acquisition."

Larissa Smith joins Flynn as a strategic advisor, bringing extensive credentials in business development, defense contracting, and government-adjacent markets. Smith, CEO of Smithwell Associates, will focus on forging partnerships with prime defense contractors, maritime suppliers, and federal systems integrators, helping them leverage IntentKey signal intelligence to outmaneuver commercial infrastructure and data center competitors in the race for engineering, manufacturing, and trade talent.

"Government suppliers are competing head-to-head against booming private-sector initiatives like data center construction for a finite pool of skilled trades and technical specialists," said Larissa Smith. "IntentKey gives defense contractors an asymmetric advantage—allowing them to pinpoint real-time behavioral signals and connect with qualified candidates before their competitors do. I am excited to help scale Inuvo’s footprint across the contractor community."

Queensland, Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Graphene Manufacturing Group Ltd. (TSXV: GMG) (OTCQX: GMGMF) ("GMG" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has signed an initial service agreement with the UK Battery Industrialisation Centre ("UKBIC") (as seen in Figure 1), the United Kingdom's national battery manufacturing development facility located in Coventry, England, to carry out cell manufacturing of GMG's next generation fast charging graphene battery cells ("G®CELLS").


Figure 1: UKBIC Location and Facilities

Under the service agreement, the battery materials for the G®CELLS will be developed, manufactured and supplied by GMG from its Battery Development Centre ("BDC") in Richlands, Brisbane, Australia. The cells will then be manufactured and formed by UKBIC at its facility in Coventry. UKBIC will initially manufacture pouch cell format[1] G®CELLS, as seen in Figure 2: Pouch Cells.



Figure 2: Pouch Cell

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/8082/324865_09d93e7604424844_002full.jpg

The UKBIC agreement adds a second international cell manufacturing partner to GMG's battery program. GMG will continue to use the Battery Innovation Center of Indiana ("BIC Indiana") in the United States of America, together with its own BDC in Brisbane, to make G®CELLS. Having cell production capability across Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom is expected to increase GMG's overall cell production capacity, allow additional cell formats to be developed in parallel, and provide sample cells closer to potential customers in Europe and the United Kingdom.

Consistent with GMG's approach with BIC Indiana, GMG will pay for services rendered by UKBIC and retain all intellectual property of the G®CELLS development work. Using UKBIC's existing industrial-scale equipment allows GMG to progress cell scale-up and process development while deferring the capital expenditure of building its own large-format cell manufacturing capacity until the technology is further de-risked.

COMMENTS:

Sean Gilgunn, Managing Director of UKBIC, commented: "UKBIC was established to help battery innovators bridge the gap between promising laboratory and pilot results and industrial-scale manufacturing. We're pleased to be applying our production lines, process engineering and formation capability to build cells using GMG's materials. Partnerships like this demonstrate the role UKBIC plays in supporting international battery developers to scale up, and in strengthening the battery manufacturing ecosystem in the United Kingdom."

Craig Nicol, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of GMG, commented: "Signing with UKBIC is an important step in scaling G®CELLS to larger cell formats. Our materials will continue to be made by GMG at our Battery Development Centre in Richlands, and UKBIC will make and form the cells in Coventry. This sits alongside our ongoing work with BIC Indiana and our own cell production in Brisbane - so rather than replacing existing capabilities, it expands our manufacturing capacity and the number of formats we can deliver to customers for testing. Importantly, it also gives us a manufacturing presence in the United Kingdom and Europe, where we see strong interest in fast charging, long life battery technology. I would like to thank Sean and the UKBIC team for their support."

Bob Galyen, GMG Director and former Chief Technology Officer of CATL, commented: "Moving a new cell chemistry from small pouch cells into larger formats is where many battery technologies are truly tested, and it is the right next step for G®CELLS following the cycle life and energy efficiency results generated at BIC Indiana. UKBIC has industrial-scale equipment covering electrode manufacturing, pouch and cylindrical cell assembly, and formation, ageing and testing - exactly what is needed to learn how the GMG materials behave at production-relevant scale. Having two experienced cell manufacturing partners in BIC Indiana and UKBIC, supplied with materials from GMG's own Battery Development Centre, gives the team more opportunities to iterate on cell design and process, which is how robust, manufacturable cells are developed."

Jack Perkowski, Chairman of GMG, commented: "The Board's strategy has always been to scale G®CELLS through world-class partners rather than committing large amounts of capital to manufacturing plants before the technology is fully de-risked. UKBIC is one of the leading national battery scale-up facilities in the world, and adding it alongside BIC Indiana gives GMG two established cell manufacturing partners on two continents, supplied with materials made by GMG in Australia. This is a capital-efficient path toward commercial production and, over time, toward our longer-term goal of licensing the technology and supplying GMG materials to battery manufacturers globally. The Board will continue to support management as they execute on this next phase."

About UKBIC
The UK Battery Industrialisation Centre (UKBIC) is the UK's national battery manufacturing development facility, providing manufacturing scale-up and skills for the battery sector. The purpose-built facility in Coventry is where businesses develop their battery manufacturing processes at the scale they need to move to industrial production, and where those working in the industry can develop new skills by working on the production line alongside UKBIC's specialist teams. UKBIC's equipment covers the battery production process from mixing and coating, calendering and slitting, to cylindrical and pouch cell assembly, formation, ageing and testing, and module and pack assembly. Opened in July 2021, UKBIC was established by the UK Government through the Faraday Battery Challenge (now the Battery Innovation Programme), delivered by UK Research and Innovation. For more information visit www.ukbic.co.uk.

Please see the following webpage for further details about the graphene batteries: https://graphenemg.com/graphene-products/gcells/. The G®CELLS are in pouch format - as seen in Figure 3. The launch video link for G®CELLS is shown in Figure 4.

About BIC Indiana
BIC Indiana is a collaborative initiative designed to incorporate leadership from renowned universities, government agencies, and commercial enterprises. BIC is a public-private partnership and a not-for-profit organization focusing on the rapid development, testing and commercialization of safe, reliable and lightweight energy storage systems for defense and commercial customers. BIC is a unique organization that has been leading battery cell development for world leading battery companies for over 10 years and has carried out over 500 battery development projects.

About GMG
GMG is an Australian based clean-technology company which develops, makes and sells energy saving and energy storage solutions, enabled by graphene manufactured via in house production process. GMG uses its own proprietary production process to decompose natural gas (i.e. methane) into its natural elements, carbon (as graphene), hydrogen and some residual hydrocarbon gases. This process produces high quality, low cost, scalable, 'tuneable' and low/no contaminant graphene suitable for use in clean-technology and other applications.

The Company's present focus is to de-risk and develop commercial scale-up capabilities, and secure market applications. In the energy savings segment, GMG has initially focused on graphene enhanced heating, ventilation and air conditioning ("HVAC-R") coating (or energy-saving coating) which is now being marketed into other applications including electronic heat sinks, industrial process plants and data centres. Another product GMG has developed is the graphene lubricant additive focused on saving liquid fuels initially for diesel engines. Smith to focus on delivering autonomy to defense customers for the next century of flight

BOSTON, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Merlin, Inc. (Nasdaq: MRLN), an aerospace and defense technology company building the operating system of record for autonomous flight, today announced that its Board of Directors has appointed Bob Smith, a member of the Board, as Chairman and Interim Chief Executive Officer, effective November 18, 2026. Smith succeeds founder Matt George, who has resigned as Chief Executive Officer, Chairman, and a member of the Board of Directors and has transitioned to the role of Founder and Advisor. 

Smith brings more than three decades of aerospace and defense leadership. As Chief Executive Officer of Blue Origin from 2017 to 2024, he transitioned the company from a research organization into an operating business, growing annual sales from nearly zero to more than $750 million and building an order book of approximately $10 billion. Previously, he spent more than a decade at Honeywell Aerospace, including as President of Mechanical Systems and Components, a business with more than $4 billion in annual revenue, and as Chief Technology Officer, responsible for more than 12,000 engineers and technologists. Prior to Honeywell, he worked on upgrading the NASA space shuttle at United Space Alliance. He also currently serves as a Senior Advisor to the Office of the Secretary of Defense as part of the Business Operators for National Defense (BOND) program and as a director of Parsons Corporation.

“Matt and this team built something incredibly novel and needed, and I’m thankful for Matt’s vision and leadership. Merlin’s autonomy software is flying today, and as we enter our next phase, our priorities are clear: deliver for our customers, including USSOCOM and AFRICOM programs; grow our pipeline; keep building Merlin Pilot; and invest with discipline to protect our strong balance sheet. It’s a great team, and I’m eager to get to work,” said Bob Smith.

“Merlin has enormous potential, and Bob is exactly the proven leader we need to unlock it,” said Michael Blitzer, Lead Independent Director of Merlin’s Board of Directors. “Having served as CEO of one of the world’s largest aerospace companies, he brings a powerful combination of commercial acumen to accelerate revenue growth and operational discipline to fundamentally improve our cost structure. Bob has a proven track record of building and leading businesses at scale, and I’m confident he is the right person to transform Merlin’s trajectory, drive sustainable profitability, and create significant long-term shareholder value. The Board is commencing a search for a permanent CEO and will consider both internal and external candidates.”

“Building Merlin with this team has been the privilege of my career. Together we took autonomy from an idea to aircraft flying for real customers. I’m proud of what we’ve built, and I’m confident Merlin is in good hands,” said Matt George.

About Merlin
Merlin is an aerospace and defense technology company building the operating system of record for autonomous flight. Through a first-principles approach, the company is redefining what’s possible across aviation, aerospace, and defense with the goal of delivering full-stack autonomy for any aircraft, military or civilian, from takeoff to touchdown. The Merlin Pilot system powers a growing range of aircraft and mission profiles, proven through hundreds of autonomous flights from test facilities across the globe. With $100M+ total in IDIQ contract ceiling value under its C-130J autonomy program with USSOCOM, Merlin is advancing American leadership in autonomous aviation by helping to solve national security challenges through safe, reliable autonomy. To learn more, visit www.merlinlabs.com or follow us on X @merlinaero.

Liver and intestinal toxicology testing both grew in the quarter ended September 30, 2026. VivoSim anticipates that the customer will make NAMkind™ testing part of its regular flow of ongoing preclinical work

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VivoSim Labs, Inc. (Nasdaq: VIVS) (the “Company” or “VivoSim”), a provider of next-generation New Approach Methodologies (NAM) 3D human cellular models for preclinical safety and efficacy testing, today announced a seven-figure agreement with a top-10 global pharmaceutical company (the “Customer”) for NAMkind™ testing services. With this agreement, the Company expects fiscal 2027 revenue to exceed the guidance of 500%+ growth it issued on July 15, 2026.

  • The agreement covers NAMkind™ liver and intestinal toxicology testing, with work already underway. Revenue under the agreement is expected to be recognized in VivoSim’s fiscal Q3 and Q4, ending Dec. 31 and March 31, respectively.
  • After this program, VivoSim anticipates that NAMkind™ testing will become part of the Customer's regular flow of ongoing preclinical work.
  • The Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, filed on November 12, shows growth in both its liver toxicology and intestinal toxicology businesses.
  • Growth came from both large pharma and smaller customers. Other current and future customers are also expected to move toward full integration of NAMkind™ testing into their workflows

How a Large Customer Adopts a New Test

A large pharmaceutical company (>$10B in annual revenue) does not quickly change how it tests drug candidates and requires extensive scientific due diligence to consider this kind of agreement. It then runs a new model on compounds whose clinical outcomes it already knows, compares the results with what its animal studies showed, and only then commits live program work. The agreement announced today covers that program work. Once it is complete, the Company anticipates that the Customer's compounds will come to VivoSim as the Customer's programs reach the relevant decision point, rather than as one-off studies.

“In July we told shareholders revenue would grow more than 500% this fiscal year. The quarterly report we filed last week shows both toxicology businesses growing, and this agreement on its own is expected to take us past that number,” said Keith Murphy, Executive Chairman of VivoSim Labs. “What matters more is what comes after it. A top-10 company has gone from evaluating our human liver and intestine models to paying for program work, and we expect its regular testing to follow. Other large customers are moving the same way.”

Since the Quarter Closed

On October 21, VivoSim added efficacy testing on disease models built from the liver and intestinal cells of patient donors, with pharmacodynamic and target biomarker profiling. On November 3, it entered a collaboration with Chemveda Life Sciences, which makes AI-designed compounds that VivoSim will then test in its human tissue models, with first programs expected to begin this quarter. This week, the Company's scientists are presenting new data demonstrating the practical impact on clinical derisking for clients of its multiparametric approach at the American College of Toxicology 47th Annual Meeting in San Antonio, Texas. The Company’s leadership is also meeting with current and prospective partners at the conference.

What Customers Are Buying

NAMkind™ liver and intestine models are built from primary human cells and dosed repeatedly over weeks. Across a clinical dataset of 92 small-molecule compounds, the NAMkind™ Liver model predicted drug-induced liver injury with 91% accuracy, 90% sensitivity and 95% specificity, whereas animal models and traditional methods typically detect 50% to 65% of true liver toxicants. Data presented at EUROTOX 2026 in September added further results in antibody-drug conjugates. Also in September, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a direct final rule clarifying that non-animal methods may be used, where appropriate, to test the safety of drugs and biologics.

“Both toxicology service lines grew in the September quarter, with orders from large pharmaceutical companies and from smaller biotechs,” said Tony Lialin, Chief Commercial Officer of VivoSim Labs. “A large customer comes in through an evaluation, then a paid program, then its standing workflow. This Customer is at the second step, and we have others at the first.”

About VivoSim Labs

VivoSim Labs, Inc. (“VivoSim” and the “Company”), is a pharmaceutical and biotechnology services company that is focused on providing testing of drugs and drug candidates in three-dimensional (“3D”) human tissue models of liver and intestine. The Company offers partners liver and intestinal toxicology insights using its new approach methodologies (“NAM”) models. The Company anticipates accelerated adoption of human tissue models following the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) Roadmap to refine animal testing requirements in favor of these non-animal NAM methods. VivoSim Labs operates from San Diego, CA. Visit www.vivosim.ai.

Integrated hardware and software solutions will enhance customer experiences, optimize cash management and support new physical and digital journeys for consumers across Australia

NORTH CANTON, Ohio, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Diebold Nixdorf (NYSE: DBD) announced that National Australia Bank (NAB) is modernizing customer experiences across its self-service network with more than 700 DN Series® cash recycling ATMs combined with the company's next-generation Vynamic® Acquiring platform. 

Through 2028, NAB will upgrade its ATMs while transforming the software infrastructure that supports physical and digital transactions. Vynamic Acquiring is built on Diebold Nixdorf's Vynamic Transaction Middleware platform and uses cloud-native, microservices-based architecture. The solution will help NAB modernize its switching environment, support regulatory compliance and introduce new customer journeys. 

NAB's ATMs support more than 500,000 transactions each week, underscoring the continued importance of convenient, dependable cash access alongside digital and in-branch banking. The initiative will:

  • Improve availability across NAB's network with modern, highly reliable ATMs, with at least two at most branches.
  • Streamline the cash cycle by securely reusing deposited banknotes for future withdrawals, reducing replenishment needs.
  • Deliver a significantly improved customer experience through clearer screens, faster processing and additional accessibility and language options.
  • Reduce ATM disputes and improve resolution outcomes by increasing visibility into cash transactions, user interactions and deposits and withdrawals.

ATM monitoring, diagnostics, services and maintenance will be provided by ITS, Diebold Nixdorf's licensed partner in Australia.

Paul Carter, Executive Retail Banking at National Australia Bank at National Australia Bank, said: "Our investment in Diebold Nixdorf's cash recycling ATMs and payments middleware strengthens our commitment to providing convenient, dependable cash access and the best customer experience in this market for individuals and small businesses across Australia. By automating more cash-handling processes, improving cash availability and reducing operational interventions, we can serve customers more dependably and efficiently wherever and whenever they need access to their money."

Jaivinder Singh Gill, senior vice president and managing director, Banking and Retail - APMEA at Diebold Nixdorf, said: "NAB's modernization shows how self-service technology and software can strengthen critical banking infrastructure while creating more connected customer experiences. We are proud to partner with NAB on this nationwide transformation, combining intelligent cash recycling technology, advanced payments software and local expertise to make everyday banking more convenient, secure and reliable."

At National Australia Bank (NAB) Group, our ambition is to be the most customer-centric company in Australia and New Zealand. More than 41,000 colleagues at the bank provide 10 million customers with secure, easy and reliable banking services. From AI campuses to U.S. Army bases: AZIO joins prime contractor ERP on two awarded U.S. Army microgrid contracts totaling about $144.6 million, including options. AZIO is general contractor at Fort Buchanan (about $45.0 million) and provides project-management support at Lake City (about $99.6 million); work begins upon delivery and acceptance of ERP’s performance and payment bonds

Different mission. Same execution. The on-site power AZIO builds for AI compute, now designed to keep U.S. Army installations running when the grid goes down.

HOUSTON, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- via IBN -- AZIO AI Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: AZIO) (“AZIO” or the “Company”) today announced it has signed a general contracting agreement with Energy Resilience Partners, LLC (“ERP”), which builds microgrids for U.S. military installations, to help deliver two awarded U.S. Army microgrid contracts. The agreement comes as the Department of War moves to put its military bases on military owned power: on Sept. 30, 2026, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced FORTRESS America, a future program that calls for every U.S. military installation to eventually run under its own power. ERP’s two contracts were awarded before that announcement and are not FORTRESS America awards. ERP is the prime contractor on both, which have a combined value of about $144.6 million, including options exercisable by the U.S. Army for increased capacity. AZIO will serve as general contractor at Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico, and provide project-management support to ERP at the Lake City Army Ammunition Plant in Missouri. The stated contract values are the values of ERP’s prime contracts with the U.S. Army, not AZIO’s expected revenue.

Work on both contracts starts only when ERP delivers, and the U.S. Army accepts, ERP’s performance and payment bonds.

AZIO builds the power and infrastructure behind AI campuses. The U.S. Army microgrids call for the same core skills: on-site generation, battery storage, controls and operation independent of the grid. As discussed under “Where AI Infrastructure Meets National Defense” below, the U.S. military is pushing for both: microgrids that keep bases running when the grid fails, and AI data centers on federal and military land. AZIO and ERP have no AI or data-center work on any U.S. military installation. Larry G. Paige II, a director of AZIO, serves as Executive Director of ERP.

AT A GLANCE

  • ERP, as prime contractor, holds two awarded U.S. Army microgrid contracts totaling about $144.6 million, including options exercisable by the U.S. Army for increased capacity.
  • Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico (about $45.0 million): AZIO serves as general contractor.
  • Lake City Army Ammunition Plant, Missouri (about $99.6 million, 15 MW): AZIO provides project-management support to ERP.
  • Timeline: each project is expected to take about three years once it begins; work begins upon delivery and acceptance of ERP’s performance and payment bonds.

FROM AI CAMPUSES TO ARMY BASES

AZIO’s thesis is simple: the next generation of AI compute will be limited less by chips than by reliable power. Through Project Atlas, the Company is developing behind-the-meter campuses in Texas that pair on-site generation with compute. Fort Buchanan and Lake City call for the same disciplines: on-site generation, battery storage, controls and grid-independent operation. The Fort Buchanan microgrid will be designed to keep the installation running without the commercial grid for up to 14 days.

  • Same capabilities, new market: AZIO’s power and infrastructure skills, applied to awarded federal construction projects with the U.S. Army as the end customer.
  • Contracted services revenue: Once work begins, AZIO expects to recognize revenue over time as it performs, adding contract-based services revenue while Project Atlas is developed. AZIO is not providing revenue or profit projections. AZIO’s compensation depends on ERP’s performance and on payment under the U.S. Army contracts and is not guaranteed.
  • Execution experience that carries over: AZIO expects that generation, storage and combined heat and power (CHP) integration at military scale will build the track record, subcontractor base and supply relationships it needs for AI campuses.

THE ARMY WORK AND AZIO’S ROLE

ERP is the prime contractor on two awarded U.S. Army microgrid contracts for which AZIO will serve in the roles identified below under its agreement with ERP:

$45.0M
FORT BUCHANAN, PUERTO RICO · AZIO: GENERAL CONTRACTOR
Four continuous-duty 2 MW diesel generators and a 5 MWh – battery energy storage system, integrating an existing 4.65 MW solar photovoltaic array and two 275 kW wind turbines. Contract W912QR26CA025. Value includes options.		$99.6M
LAKE CITY ARMY AMMUNITION PLANT, MISSOURI · AZIO: PROJECT-MANAGEMENT SUPPORT
A 15 MW microgrid and combined heat and power project, with two 7.5 MW CHP combustion turbines. Contract W912QR26CA040. Value includes options.		 

Under the general contracting agreement with ERP, AZIO’s compensation consists of its costs plus a fee at Fort Buchanan, and a management fee plus reimbursable costs at Lake City.

POWER THAT DOESN’T BLINK

When the grid fails, everything plugged into it can fail too.

In February 2021, Winter Storm Uri cut power to more than 4.5 million people in Texas, some for as long as four days, and ERCOT ordered 20,000 MW of rolling blackouts to keep the grid from collapsing (FERC and NERC, February 2021 Cold Weather Outages report, Nov. 2021). On April 28, 2025, continental Spain and Portugal went into a total blackout (ENTSO-E). In December 2024, a utility power loss at a Microsoft Azure datacenter in the South Central United States took down compute, network and storage in one data hall after it failed to transfer to backup power. In February 2023, a utility voltage dip at a Microsoft Azure facility in Southeast Asia caused a cooling failure and a shutdown of critical infrastructure.

AZIO believes military installations and AI campuses are better served by power they generate on site.

WHERE AI INFRASTRUCTURE MEETS NATIONAL DEFENSE

On Sept. 30, 2026, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced FORTRESS America, a future Department of War program that calls for every U.S. military installation to eventually run under its own power (U.S. Department of War, war.gov, Sept. 30, 2026). The U.S. Army has stated a goal of installing a microgrid on every installation by 2035 (U.S. Army Climate Strategy, February 2022, Intermediate Objective 1.1). Federal law directs the Secretary of War to pursue energy security and energy resilience (10 U.S.C. § 2911).

The same policy push now reaches AI infrastructure. Executive Order 14318 (July 23, 2025) directs the Secretary of War to identify suitable sites on U.S. military installations and competitively lease land for qualifying data center and related energy projects. The Department of Energy has selected four of its sites, Idaho National Laboratory, Oak Ridge Reservation, Paducah and Savannah River, for private AI data center and energy projects (DOE, July 24, 2025). In March 2026, the U.S. Army conditionally selected developers to negotiate leases for commercial hyperscale data centers at Fort Bliss, Texas, and Dugway Proving Ground, Utah, and said those developers will build and operate behind-the-meter power and water systems; the leases are not final (U.S. Army, March 26, 2026). The Pentagon’s fiscal 2027 budget request seeks about $29.5 billion for an “AI Arsenal” initiative of secure data centers and AI supercomputers, subject to congressional approval (DefenseScoop, May 22, 2026, citing DoD budget documents).

AZIO is not a party to any of these programs, and neither AZIO nor ERP has AI or data-center work on any military installation. The two ERP contracts are microgrid construction contracts awarded before FORTRESS America was announced; they are not FORTRESS America or AI awards. AZIO cites these developments as industry context: the on-site generation, storage and controls these programs call for are the capabilities behind-the-meter AI campuses require.

MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY

“Energy resilience is national security, and reliable power is the foundation of everything we build, whether it serves an AI campus or a U.S. Army installation. Different mission, same execution: the on-site generation, microgrid controls and off-grid resilience behind our AI campuses are exactly what these U.S. Army microgrids call for. These are awarded projects with defined scopes and schedules. We are the general contractor at Fort Buchanan, and we are helping ERP run Lake City. Our job is to get to the starting line, which means getting ERP’s bonds accepted so work can start. From there, our focus is delivering safely, on time and on budget for ERP and the U.S. Army, and bringing that experience back to our AI infrastructure work,” said Chris Young, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of AZIO.

ABOUT AZIO AI HOLDINGS, INC.

AZIO AI Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: AZIO), formerly Envirotech Vehicles, Inc. (Nasdaq: EVTV), is a technology infrastructure company focused on developing, owning, and operating artificial intelligence compute campuses, enterprise GPU compute infrastructure, digital power solutions, and other high compute operations. Through Project Atlas, the Company is developing behind-the-meter, power-backed campuses in Texas intended to support power-intensive compute workloads as additional generation, connectivity, customer commitments, and capital are secured.
